slides.heading: Iterative In Order Traversal
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Iterative In Order Traversal, a very hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: In-order traversal with O(1) extra space using parent pointers.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. In-order traversal with constant extra space using parent pointers.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Parent pointers let us know where we came from, so we can walk without a stack.
slides.narration: Parent pointers let us know where we came from, so we can walk without a stack.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Recursion and explicit stacks both use height space. With parent pointers, tracking the previous node is enough for constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Coming from parent, go left if possible
3. Coming from left, visit then go right
slides.narration: Step by step. First, track previous and current. Second, coming from parent, go left if possible. Third, coming from left, visit then go right. Fourth, coming from right, go up.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Use parent pointers, no stack
slides.narration: With parent pointers, we can traverse in-order using only prev and current.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: came from parent → go left if possible, else visit & go right/up
came from left child → visit, go right or up
came from right child → go up

slides.caption: Three cases by where we came from
slides.narration: If we came from the parent, go left if we can, else visit and go right or up. From the left child, visit and go right or up. From the right child, go up.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Visit order 4, 2, 1, 6, 3, 7
slides.narration: That yields the in-order sequence four, two, one, six, three, seven.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We loop while current exists, choose next by the three cases, calling the callback at the right moments, then shift prev and current.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Distinguish arriving from left vs right
Stop when we step past the root's parent
slides.narration: Carefully distinguish arriving from the left child versus the right.
